source_text.body:
Fill forms and scan Marketplace with a browser agent
A user used Comet to fill forms, complete compliance trainings, and scan Facebook Marketplace, though it recently began refusing those agentic tasks.
·
Jan 1, 2025
Done with
PC
Perplexity Comet
What they did
The poster says they had been using Perplexity’s Comet browser assistant widely to act on webpages for tasks like filling forms, doing compliance trainings, and scanning Facebook Marketplace listings. In the thread, other users describe the assistant controlling the browser, with people still stepping in for things like login or captchas, but several commenters say the stronger agentic behavior was moved behind Perplexity’s paid Computer feature or higher-tier plans.
How it went
The reported outcome is mixed: the original user says those workflows stopped working over the prior couple of weeks, while one Enterprise Max user says browser-control tasks still work satisfactorily more often than not. No hard performance numbers are given; the main shortfall is reduced willingness or ability to take actions on sites.
Worth knowing
The main catch in the comments is pricing and access: multiple users say the more capable browser automation was shifted behind Computer or Enterprise/Max tiers.
Try it yourself
with
Perplexity Comet
Copy prompt
Open [website or form URL] and fill out the form using these details: [your info]. Stop on the final page before submitting and show me everything you entered so I can confirm. Separately, scan [marketplace site] for [item] within [distance] of [location] under $[price] and list the 5 best listings with price, location, and link.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/perplexity_ai/comments/1vfh1nw/what_happened_to_comet_why_did_it_become_so
